source.operator: Thames Gateway Waste to Energy Limited

rows.finding: The application reference is EPR/CP3737CV/V003 and the consolidated permit number is EPR/CP3737CV.
The variation application was duly made on 18 March 2015.
The installation was described as being on a brownfield site within an Air Quality Management Area at London Sustainable Industries Park.
The decision document centres the installation on National Grid Reference TQ 4834 8289.
The Environment Agency decided to grant the variation subject to the consolidated permit conditions.
The varied installation activity is Section 5.1 Part A(1)(b), incineration of non-hazardous waste at 3 tonnes or more per hour.
Before the variation the installation activity was Section 5.1 Part A(1)(a), incineration of hazardous waste.
The proposed gasification technology changed from Cyclamax SBOS to Chinook Sciences RODECS.
Permitted annual waste processing was proposed to increase from 120,000 to 180,000 tonnes per year.
Hazardous and clinical wastes were removed from the acceptable waste list under the variation.
The process stages are gasification, syngas combustion, waste-heat steam generation and steam-turbine electricity generation.
The installation uses two process lines, each with a design capacity of 90,000 tonnes per year.
Each RODECS bin has a target batch weight of approximately 24 tonnes.
Maximum waste stored for treatment was specified as 1,980 tonnes.
The 1,980-tonne storage capacity was described as approximately 3.5 days of input at 7,500 operating hours per year.
Waste was not to be stored for more than seven days from receipt.
The RODECS option table gives annual availability of 7,500 hours.
Total power generation for the RODECS option was stated as 147,000 MWh per year.
Power consumed by the RODECS option was stated as 33,195 MWh per year.
Net power exported to the grid was stated as 113,805 MWh per year.
Average net power export was stated as 15.17 MWe per hour.
The option table reports a net figure of 146,177 tonnes of carbon dioxide reduced.
The net CO2-reduction figure includes direct stack CO2 minus avoided landfill gas, displaced grid electricity and avoided primary metal smelting.
The operator stated an estimated 35,000 tonnes CO2 per year for the proposed technology in its energy and GWP assessment.
The decision document compares the 35,000-tonne estimate with a 150,000-tonne CO2-per-year RGN8 surrogate level for a substantial release.
The decision states that the principal greenhouse gas emitted is carbon dioxide.
Small amounts of nitrous oxide were expected from secondary NOx abatement.
The 2015 decision used a nitrous-oxide global warming potential of 310 times CO2.
The major greenhouse-gas source was identified as CO2 from waste combustion.
Additional CO2 sources include support fuels used at startup, shutdown and to maintain combustion temperature.
BAT for greenhouse-gas emissions was described as maximising energy recovery and efficiency.
The installation was stated not to be subject to the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme Regulations 2012 at the time of the decision.
Waste-combustion CO2 is listed on the GWP debit side.
Auxiliary or supplementary fuel CO2 is listed on the GWP debit side.
CO2 associated with electrical energy use is listed on the GWP debit side.
N2O from the de-NOx process is listed on the GWP debit side.
Displacement of virgin-fuel electricity generation by exported electricity is listed on the GWP credit side.
Avoided methane from waste that might otherwise have been landfilled was explicitly excluded from the cited assessment section.
When landfill effects were included, the operator assessment found RODECS better than SBOS for GWP.
rows.value: RODECS preferred for GWP with landfill effects

rows.finding: The Environment Agency agreed that the chosen RODECS option was BAT for the installation.

quality_gate: Permit decisions, design values, modelled avoided emissions and operator estimates are not PRTR or Pollution Inventory measured facility releases. Facility publication requires an official reporting-year pollutant value and unit; parcel attribution additionally requires verified HMLR geometry.
